questions.story: A customer sends a screenshot of a fake payment alert claiming money was transferred to your account and asks for immediate product dispatch.
questions.question: What process control prevents sending goods based on fraudulent payment notifications?
options: Dispatching the order immediately to maintain customer satisfaction
Out-of-band verification (checking your official banking or Mobile Money app directly before releasing goods)
Replying to the customer asking if the screenshot is real
questions.feedback: Never rely on customer-provided screenshots or SMS alerts; always verify funds directly inside your official financial app.

questions.story: Attackers send fake SMS alerts mimicking official Mobile Money or bank deposit receipts.
questions.question: What technical indicator helps distinguish real transactional alerts from spoofed SMS messages?
options: Checking if the SMS came from a standard 10-digit personal phone number instead of an official registered Sender ID
Checking if the text message contains emojis
Reading the SMS twice to see if the wording changes
questions.feedback: Spoofed SMS payment alerts are frequently sent from regular personal mobile numbers rather than verified corporate Sender IDs.

questions.story: An employee receives a suspicious notification claiming an order payment was reversed.
questions.question: Which automated security setting alerts the business to unauthorized attempts to modify store account settings?
options: Real-time SMS/Email alerts for administrative account modifications and payment gateway setting updates
Manually auditing bank statements at the end of the year
questions.feedback: Real-time administrative alerts notify owners immediately if an attacker attempts to alter connected payout details.

questions.story: A fraudster claims they overpaid for an item and demands an immediate refund via a separate Mobile Money transfer.
questions.question: What security policy protects your business from overpayment refund fraud?
options: Sending cash back immediately via a personal phone number
Enforcing a policy where refunds are only issued through official payment gateway channels after full bank settlement verification
Asking a coworker to pay the refund out of pocket
Ignoring the customer entirely without checking statements
questions.feedback: Overpayment scams rely on sense of urgency; refunding through unverified channels before bank settlement results in direct financial loss.
